mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Registration (equivalent to Certificate of Incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean District Court Registration Office having jurisdiction over the registered office, e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registration Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain the court-issued certificate; have the registry officer's signature notarized by a Korean notary public; if the destination state is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, obtain an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea; if the destination is not an Apostille party, complete consular legalization through the Korean consular post and the destination state's embassy. The Apostille route and the consular legalization route are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Current Corporate Registration Status and Tax Compliance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service (NTS) and the competent district registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain the original tax clearance and corporate status extract; notarize the certifying officer's signature; for Hague Apostille member states, affix the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille; for non-member states, apply for consular legalization at the Korean diplomatic mission and the receiving state's consulate. These two authentication mechanisms are strictly alternative, not sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the Founding Members and Notarized Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Yuhan Hoesa founding members / Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute the resolution and power of attorney before a Korean notary; notarize the signatures; if the destination country is an Apostille Convention member, obtain the Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs; otherwise, use consular legalization through the Korean consulate and the destination embassy. Apostille and consular legalization are exclusive alternatives and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Memorandum and Articles of the Yuhan Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public and the company's founding members
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Register the Articles of Association with the registry and obtain a certified duplicate; notarize the duplicate; then either obtain a Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille if the receiving state is an Apostille party, or complete consular legalization if the receiving state is not an Apostille party. The two routes are mutually exclusive and must not be executed sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a Korean Commercial Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Korean commercial bank maintaining the corporate current account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Request the bank reference letter on bank letterhead signed by an authorized bank officer; notarize the bank officer's signature; if the destination jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille state, obtain the Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs; if it is a non-member state, complete consular legalization through the Korean consular post and the destination embassy. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel, mutually exclusive paths and must not be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All natural and legal persons who ultimately, alone or jointly, hold 25% or more of the membership interests, or who otherwise exercise control over the Yuhan Hoesa, must be screened before incorporation and periodically thereafter against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UK HM Treasury Consolidated List, the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit Watchlist, and domestic police watchlists. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any politically exposed person, family member, or close associate; source of funds, beneficial ownership, and commercial rationale must be documented in writing by the Korean FIU compliance officer or external AML counsel.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS) corporate name search and reservation system at www.iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All statutory corporate names must be registered in Hangeul. The English transliteration must follow the Revised Romanization of Korean system administered by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism. The registered name must include the legal form suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa' and must comply with the four-tier naming convention: jurisdiction and entity type marker, distinctive element, business descriptor, and legal form suffix. The English name is a transliteration for cross-border convenience and cannot create an independent legal name or bypass the Hangeul registration requirement.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must file a written objection with the head of the competent registration office within 14 days from the date of notification, attaching the search report from IROS, the rejected application, and a cover letter explaining the proposed name's distinctiveness. If the rejection was based on a prohibited or sensitive token, the applicant must submit evidence of prior ministerial approval or legal exemption. If the objection is dismissed, an administrative appeal may be filed with the competent District Court within 90 days under the Administrative Litigation Act. All appeal documents must be signed by a Korean-authorized representative and, if necessary, notarized.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure mailbox-only virtual office is generally rejected by the National Tax Service and Korean commercial banks for a wholesale bitumen and asphalt logistics trading LLC. The NTS requires an actual place of business where books, records, contracts, and import/export logistics documentation can be examined. A serviced office with physical signage, a dedicated work station, lease documentation, and storage for corporate records may be accepted, but banks will still require a site visit, a lease contract, a utility bill, and evidence that the registered address is not used exclusively for mail forwarding. The entity should maintain an operating address with tangible business activity to pass customs and tax substance reviews.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced physical inspection: (1) company nameplate visible at the registered address; (2) current lease or occupancy agreement; (3) physical or digital ledgers and contracts related to containerized asphalt; (4) VAT registration confirmation tied to the address; (5) staff or a registered manager available during business hours; (6) evidence that the office is not a mere mailbox. Quantified risk: medium-to-high, approximately 50-60%, for an entity relying solely on a virtual mailbox within the first 12 months; low-to-medium, approximately 10-15%, for a genuine serviced office with active operational records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Book III, Chapter VII governing Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company), Articles 601 through 624, together with the general corporate registration provisions of Book III, Chapter I; also the Registration of Real Estate and Companies Act for commercial registration procedure and the Local Tax Act for registration tax assessment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the Korean District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the Company's registered office; electronic filing through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IROS) at www.iros.go.kr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration of a Limited Liability Company (Commercial Registration Application) accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation and certified statutory exhibits.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Commercial Act. The Company has no statutory minimum paid-up capital; the founders must nevertheless declare a capital amount in the Articles of Incorporation. All cash contributions must be deposited into a subscription bank account opened in the name of the prospective company or held with an escrow/blocked account instruction before registration. Such funds are legally blocked and may not be withdrawn or disbursed for corporate use until the District Court completes incorporation registration, except for refund to subscribers if incorporation fails. Contributions in kind must be fully transferred to the Company and verified by a court-appointed appraiser. Registration tax is separately assessed by the local government on the declared capital; because capital is not fixed in this payload, no single official USD fee amount is stated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) TAKEN BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE INITIAL DIRECTORS AND MEMBERS UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA AND THE COMPANY'S ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION.

WHEREAS the Articles of Incorporation of the Company have been duly executed, notarized, and registered with the competent District Court; and

WHEREAS the entire share capital subscribed under the Articles of Incorporation has been lawfully subscribed by the members and fully paid into the duly blocked subscription bank account or otherwise contributed in kind as verified by the court-appointed appraiser; and

WHEREAS the registered office address has been obtained under lease, and the leasehold documents, landlord consent, and building registry extracts have been prepared for statutory filing; and

WHEREAS the Company intends to engage in the wholesale supply of drummed and bagged penetration grade bitumen and asphalt logistics trading under ISIC 4661 and needs banking arrangements, statutory officers, and ancillary licenses to operate lawfully;

NOW, THEREFORE, the Board of Directors hereby resolves as follows:

1. Subscription of Share Capital and Acknowledgment of Payment. The directors acknowledge that the share capital of the Company stated in the Articles of Incorporation is fully subscribed. Each member has paid the amount of his or her contribution in full, and the bank deposit certificates, blocked-funds confirmations, or in-kind contribution appraisal reports are accepted and placed in the corporate minute book. No further capital call is currently outstanding.

2. Banking Authorization. The Company shall open its primary corporate operating account at a commercial bank duly licensed in the Republic of Korea. The Representative Director, jointly with the Finance Director or other designated officer, is hereby exclusively authorized to execute account opening documents, banking mandates, corporate seal cards, SWIFT TT instructions, letter of credit applications, electronic banking registration, and all related treasury documents. Any transaction above the internal control threshold requires dual officer approval.

3. Adoption of Registered Office. The registered office of the Company is hereby fixed and adopted at the lease address described in the Articles of Incorporation. The Representative Director is directed to present the lease agreement, landlord confirmation, and proof of address to the District Court, National Tax Service, and all competent licensing authorities. Any change of registered office shall require a subsequent board resolution and court registration.

4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The Board appoints the initial Representative Director, Directors, and if applicable, the statutory Auditor. Each appointee has affirmatively accepted office in writing. The Representative Director and Directors are jointly authorized to execute statutory filings, tax registrations, employment registrations, and to apply for petroleum wholesale registration, environmental approvals, fire safety permits, and all permits necessary for wholesale distribution of bitumen and asphalt products.

5. Ratification of Incorporation Acts. All acts performed by the incorporators and initial subscribers before and in connection with incorporation registration, including the opening of the subscription account and execution of the lease, are hereby ratified, approved, and confirmed.

This resolution is immediately effective and remains in force until varied by a subsequent resolution of the Company's appropriate governing body. Duly passed and entered into the corporate minute book this day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean notary public; subsequent filing through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IROS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators must prepare and execute Articles of Incorporation in writing, stating the corporate name, corporate purpose, registered office location, declared capital, contribution units and amounts, method of contribution, initial officers, and fiscal year end. The business purpose clause must explicitly include the wholesale supply, storage, logistics, and trading of drummed and bagged penetration grade bitumen and asphalt products under ISIC 4661. All incorporators must appear before or submit signed and sealed documents to a licensed notary, who shall verify identity, authority, and capacity. The notary confirms that the Articles are not contrary to law and affixes the notarial certificate. Foreign shareholders must deliver notarized powers of attorney, passport copies, and, for corporate shareholders, apostilled certificates of incorporation and good standing.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean or bilingual format
Notarized power of attorney for each incorporator
Passport or national identity card of each member
Certificate of good standing and apostilled corporate extract for non-resident corporate shareholders
Detailed business purpose statement covering ISIC 4661 wholesale bitumen and asphalt logistics
Local contact address and Korean-language service/inspection officer appointment form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises an objection to capital valuation, purpose ambiguity, or foreign document authentication, the incorporators shall correct the Articles and re-execute with conformed signatures. For foreign documents lacking apostille, the remedy is to obtain apostille from the issuing state or use consular legalization, with a 10-business-day cure period before re-presentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of share capital into blocked subscription bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed in the Republic of Korea and regulated by the Financial Supervisory Service; notarial escrow if bank refuses temporary subscription deposit.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commercial registration, the incorporators shall open a temporary or subscription bank account in the name of the Company or for the benefit of the Company. The full amount of declared cash capital must be wired or deposited into that account. The bank is instructed to mark the account as blocked and to issue a certificate of deposit and frozen funds showing the account name, deposit date, amount, and the restriction that funds may not be withdrawn until presentation of the completed certificate of incorporation registration. For contributions in kind, a court-appointed appraiser must verify the value and the asset transfer documents. The deposit certificate is then kept with the corporate records and later annexed to the registration application.
required_dossiers: Subscription bank account application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Passport or registration certificate of each subscriber
Statement of foreign remittance or source-of-funds evidence
Bank deposit certificate and blocked-funds confirmation
In-kind contribution appraisal report and transfer deed, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced due diligence or asks for further corporate documentation, the incorporators shall supply a legal opinion on the corporate formation and source of funds. If the bank refuses to issue a blocked-funds certificate, the incorporators shall place the capital in notarial escrow and obtain a notarial escrow certificate, which equally satisfies the registration examiner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation registration with the District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; electronic filing via IROS portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After completion of the bank deposit and notarization, the representative incorporator or its attorney shall submit the commercial registration application through IROS or in person to the court registry. The application must state the corporate name, business purpose, address, capital, members, contribution amounts and methods, officers, and representation authority. The registry reviews the notarized Articles, deposit certificate, officer consents, proof of registered office, and payment of registration tax and education surcharge. Registration tax is assessed on declared capital under local tax law; court registry fees are paid by electronic stamp. Upon issuance of the Corporate Registration Certificate and certified registry extract, the Company becomes a legal entity. The registry will return certified extracts and corporate seal registration is next.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration application form
Certified true copy of notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank blocked-funds certificate or notarial escrow certificate
In-kind contribution appraisal report and transfer proof, if applicable
Statutory consent forms of directors and auditor
Registered office lease agreement and landlord consent
Power of attorney for the agent and identity documents
Payment receipt for registration tax and local education surcharge
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues an inquiry or corrective instruction, the applicant shall answer through IROS within the statutory correction period, pay any shortfall of registration tax, and re-submit the corrected registration application. If the examiner challenges the blocked deposit, the applicant shall provide a supplemental bank statement and a legal memorandum proving that the corporate capital remains available and legally restricted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service business registration and corporate tax enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local branch of the National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax online portal; relevant local tax office under the Ministry of the Interior and Safety for local taxes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of court registration, the Company must apply for a Business Registration Certificate from the NTS using the certified corporate registration extract. The application must also register for corporate income tax, value-added tax, withholding on wages and domestic payments, and, for foreign shareholders, non-resident tax withholding obligations. The NTS will issue the Company's unique business registration number. The same registration file is used by the local government for annual property taxes, local income tax, and employment insurance administration. The Company should also register with the National Pension Service, health insurance, employment insurance, and workers compensation insurance through the integrated social insurance system.
required_dossiers: NTS business registration application form
Certified extract of corporate registration from the court
Corporate seal certificate or corporate seal registration card
Lease agreement and proof of registered office
Passport or ID of the representative director
Bank account opening certificate in the corporate name
Power of attorney and tax agent appointment if filed through a tax representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS requests verification of the registered office or shareholder beneficial ownership, the Company shall submit the lease certificate, bank statements, and a shareholder register. If the business registration certificate is delayed, the Company may use the receipt notice as temporary evidence and may bind commercial customers by issuing an advance tax invoice after receiving the certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate seal registration and physical/industrial licensing for bitumen wholesale storage
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division for corporate seal; provincial city/do petroleum licensing window delegated by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy; local fire department; Ministry of Environment; Ministry of Employment and Labor and Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency (KOSHA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, the Company must register its corporate seal with the competent court registry office to obtain a Corporate Seal Certificate, which is required for banking, contracts, customs, and licenses. For the physical wholesale and containerized storage of bitumen and asphalt products, the Company must additionally obtain the petroleum wholesale business registration under the Petroleum and Petroleum Substitute Fuel Business Act, and if it maintains storage for third parties or conducts warehousing as a distinct activity, a warehouse business registration under the Distribution Industry Development Act. The Company must file a small air pollution emission source registration with the local environmental authority, submit a fire safety installation plan and completion inspection application with the local fire department, and prepare a workplace risk assessment and material safety data sheet registry under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. The storage area for drums and bulk bag asphalt must have secondary containment, ventilation, and fire separation.
required_dossiers: Corporate seal registration application and notarial seal specimen
Corporate registration certificate and NTS business registration certificate
Petroleum wholesale business registration application form
Warehouse business registration application form, if separate
Storage facility layout plans and tank/drum containment drawings
Fire protection system design plan and completion inspection application
Environmental registration form for small air pollutant emission source
Material safety data sheets for bitumen and asphalt products
Workplace risk assessment report and emergency response plan
Waste management plan for bitumen residues and used containment pallets
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the petroleum registration is suspended pending facility inspection, the Company may apply for conditional approval by committing in writing to complete fire suppression, secondary containment, and emergency response upgrades within a fixed period. If the fire department identifies deficiencies, the Company should obtain a remedial action plan from a licensed fire safety engineer and resubmit within the cure period. For any licensing rejection, administrative appeal to the mayor/do governor or the central administrative appeals commission remains available.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Petroleum and chemical licensing division of the relevant Metropolitan City or Do provincial government, delegated by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE); technical inspection and monitoring by the Korea Petroleum Management Institute (K-Petroleum); local district office for business licensing; the Korea Environment Corporation (KECO) and Ministry of Environment for environmental permits; and the local fire department for civil defense and fire safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Petroleum Products Wholesale Business Registration for Bitumen and Asphalt Products under the Petroleum and Petroleum Substitute Fuel Business Act, together with Warehouse Business Registration under the Distribution Industry Development Act if the containerized bitumen storage is operated as an independent warehousing activity; the activity is not a manufacturing license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (ME) / Korea Environment Corporation (KECO) through the local environmental permit bureau; wastewater and air permits administered by regional environmental agencies.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration (Category C small-scale facility) for a drummed and bagged bitumen warehouse and wholesale distribution site; a full Environmental Impact Assessment is not triggered unless the site area exceeds 50,000 square meters or petroleum product storage capacity exceeds the threshold requiring prior environmental review under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act and the Small-Scale Environmental Impact Assessment Act. If the warehouse floor area exceeds 10,000 square meters or the total storage capacity exceeds 4,000 kiloliters, a Prior Environmental Review or Full EIA shall be required, whichever is applicable under the project classification table.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater is expected from pure containerized bitumen wholesale trading; however, any washwater or stormwater runoff from paved storage areas must meet Water Environment Conservation Act effluent limits of not more than 40 mg/L BOD, 40 mg/L COD, 40 mg/L suspended solids, 1 mg/L total phosphorus, and 0.01 mg/L total organic fluorine compounds where applicable. VOC emissions from drum venting, loading, and unloading must be controlled with vapor recovery efficiency of not less than 95% and fugitive VOC leaks below enforceable local ambient and boundary standards. Bitumen residues, asphalt sludge, oily rags, and contaminated absorbent material are designated waste under the Waste Control Act and must be stored in leak-proof covered containers with secondary containment, transferred only by licensed waste carriers, and removed to licensed treatment facilities within 90 days under the electronic waste manifest system.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The Company must obtain a Civil Defense and Firefighting Facility Completion Inspection Certificate from the local fire department, including approval of the fire alarm system, portable fire extinguishers, fire hydrants or sprinkler systems if required, emergency exit routes, and evacuation signage. Structural load certification of drum racks and storage shelving must be issued by a licensed structural engineer. Occupational safety approval is required under the Occupational Safety and Health Act through submission of material safety data sheets, chemical risk assessments, fume and ventilation control plans, personal protective equipment programs, and a heat-stress and handling plan for hot bitumen operations; high-risk workplace registration applies if heating, mixing, or hot-transfer of bitumen above 120 degrees Celsius is performed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, with electronic fiscal filings through the NTS HomeTax portal (hometax.go.kr). Customs export declarations are processed by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS system (unipass.customs.go.kr). VAT is administered centrally by the NTS; there is no sub-national or provincial VAT jurisdiction in Korea.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act at the competent district court registry and obtain the corporate registration certificate and corporate seal certificate. Step 2: If foreign investors hold equity, obtain a foreign-investment registration certificate from KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Step 3: File an 'Application for Business Registration' with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered head office within 20 days after the commencement of business under Article 24 of the Value-Added Tax Act. Step 4: Submit the articles of incorporation, corporate registration transcript, business-premises lease or ownership documentation, landlord identification or consent where applicable, corporate seal certificate, and passport or other identification for foreign shareholders. Step 5: The NTS assigns a 10-digit Business Registration Number that simultaneously serves as the corporate Tax Identification Number and the VAT registration ID. Step 6: Enroll the entity in the HomeTax electronic tax invoice system. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Korean domestic place of business, a tax representative must be designated for VAT registration and filing where Korean VAT obligations arise; however, the Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic resident corporation and follows the standard domestic registration procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not provide a check-the-box or other pass-through election for a Yuhan Hoesa. A Korean limited liability company is always treated as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act and is subject to entity-level corporate tax; it is also a general taxable person for VAT regardless of turnover.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold. Registration is mandatory from business commencement for every taxable person carrying on a trade or business in Korea. The KRW 80,000,000 annual turnover figure is relevant only to the simplified taxable person status for small individual merchants; a Yuhan Hoesa corporation is always a general taxable person and must register regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea mandates electronic tax invoicing under the Value-Added Tax Act. Tax invoices must be issued in electronic form and transmitted to the NTS through the HomeTax electronic tax invoice service, or through an authorized EDI/API solution, within the prescribed time after each supply. For export sales, the electronic tax invoice must be marked zero-rated and should reference the UNI-PASS customs export declaration number. Korea does not operate a physical fiscal stamping or fiscal printer clearance regime; instead, the NTS and Korea Customs Service automatically cross-match electronic tax invoices, customs export declarations, foreign exchange transaction records, and refund claims. Export transactions may be subjected to pre-refund verification or prior-review requests before any zero-rated VAT refund is released.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act zero-rates the export of goods. For this wholesale supply of drummed and bagged penetration grade bitumen, the Yuhan Hoesa will qualify for 0% VAT if it is the exporter of record, the goods are physically exported from the Republic of Korea to an overseas destination under the Customs Act, legal title and risk pass to the foreign buyer under the contractual Incoterms, and the export consideration is received in foreign currency from the overseas buyer. The foreign exchange must be settled within the statutory period, ordinarily 180 days from export clearance. Qualifying international transport and logistics services connected to the export are also zero-rated, but the physical export of the goods is the primary basis for the claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: UNI-PASS Customs Export Declaration and the Korea Customs Service Export Declaration Confirmation, evidencing the customs clearance number and exporter-of-record status.
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list describing the containerized drummed and bagged bitumen/asphalt, quantity, unit price, and overseas consignee.
Bill of Lading or equivalent multimodal transport document proving physical shipment from a Korean port to the foreign destination.
Foreign Exchange Transaction Confirmation and foreign currency receipt statement issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing inward remittance of the export proceeds from the overseas buyer.
Export contract or purchase order, and where requested by the NTS, the Korea Customs Service export clearance status report or cargo manifest evidence.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS actively cross-matches zero-rated VAT declarations with Korea Customs Service export data and bank foreign-exchange receipt records. If an export zero-rating claim is not substantiated by valid customs documentation, if the goods are not actually exported, or if foreign-currency proceeds are not received within the 180-day settlement period, the NTS may retrospectively disallow the zero-rating and reclassify the transaction as a taxable domestic supply. In that case, 10% VAT is assessed on the export sales price, together with additional tax under the Value-Added Tax Act, late-payment interest under the Framework Act on National Taxes, and, in cases involving fraudulent or grossly false documentation, criminal penalties under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. The ordinary statute of limitations for tax assessment is five years from the end of the relevant taxable period, extended to ten years where false or fraudulent declarations are established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as co-administrators under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a highly open capital account with full current account convertibility and a liberalised capital account subject to notification and reporting rather than prior approval. The Korean won is fully freely convertible for trade and most service transactions. Profit remittance (dividends, royalties, and interest) is permitted without central bank approval, provided the remitting entity meets tax clearance obligations under the Corporate Tax Act and submits the appropriate Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) report through a domestic foreign exchange bank. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity injections and inbound loans, require a report to the MOEF/BOK under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; however, these are typically administrative notifications with no conversion restrictions. There are no surrender requirements for export proceeds, but exporters must collect export receipts within the statutory period (generally 6 months, extendable to 12 months with approval) and report collection through an authorised foreign exchange bank. The won's exchange rate is freely floating under a market average rate system, and the BOK may intervene to smooth disorderly conditions. For a bitumen wholesale trading LLC, the principal FX hurdle is ensuring accurate documentation of the underlying physical trade (invoice, bill of lading, and payment flow) to satisfy the FEIS reporting and to avoid classification as a disguised capital transaction. Overall, the regime supports efficient treasury operations, but non-resident shareholders and foreign directors must appoint a domestic tax representative for remittance-related tax registrations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory conversion or surrender ratio for export proceeds in South Korea. Under FETA and the Customs Act, exporters must ensure that foreign currency receipts are remitted into the domestic foreign exchange bank account within a maximum of six (6) months from the date of exportation, unless an extension up to twelve (12) months is granted by the designated bank based on justifiable commercial reasons. All export proceeds must be reported through the FEIS within one (1) business day of receipt. The exporter may retain the foreign currency in a corporate foreign exchange account or convert it to KRW at the prevailing market rate; no forced conversion applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and FX)
Capital Escrow Account and Trade Settlement Account
Basic Operational Currency Account with Trade Finance Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) and offshore digital banks have very limited to negligible viability for serving a Korean-incorporated LLC engaged in bulk commodity trading. Under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act (EFTA) and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, only domestic licensed banks and financial investment companies are authorised to execute FX trades, handle outward/remittance processing, and issue trade-related guarantees for domestic corporations. Offshore EMIs such as TransferWise/Revolut are not licensed deposit-takers in Korea and cannot open a KRW settlement account for a Korean entity; they may only offer ancillary multi-currency receipts in the name of the customer, but these fail the FEIS reporting obligations and bank-grade compliance requirements for trade settlement. Consequently, the recommended treasury infrastructure relies exclusively on domestic Tier-1 commercial banks for statutory capital escrow, trade settlements, and FX hedging. Any fintech solution is limited to invoice reconciliation or expense automation and must never be used for trade payment rails because it would trigger automatic regulatory scrutiny and potential administrative penalties.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly incorporated Korean LLC whose directors may be non-residents, physical presence of the statutory director or a duly authorised representative is mandatory for the initial corporate account opening under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act. The director must appear in-branch at the designated domestic Tier-1 bank, in person, with the original certificate of corporate seal, corporate registration certificate, and director identification. Remote opening is not permitted for newly formed entities without any previous domestic banking relationship. If a director is located abroad, a notarised power of attorney (apostilled or consular-legalised) may allow a domestic representative (e.g., the corporate tax agent or a local company secretary) to attend the interview, but the bank may still require a video call with the beneficial owner to verify identity. For capital escrow accounts, the bank compliance team will conduct a face-to-face interview with the economic owner to validate source of wealth and the commercial purpose of the entity before activating any transaction volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the registered business scope (wholesale trade of bitumen/asphalt) and the expected transaction counterparties located in high-risk or unknown jurisdictions (e.g., tax-haven registrations or countries with heightened sanctions).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full commercial contract with counterparty details, Incoterms, and underlying product specifications; a corporate structure chart of the material counterparty; copies of licences for asphalt import in the destination country; and a written explanation of how the physical trade complies with the South Korean Foreign Trade Act and international sanctions screening results from a recognised KYC database (e.g., World-Check, Dow Jones).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for the initial capital injection is unclear, particularly if the inbound wire is originated from a jurisdiction with strict bank secrecy or from a private investment company without transparent beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory bank statements (6–12 months) of the funding shareholder, source-of-wealth declaration signed by the UBO, audited financial statements of the sending entity, a declaration of the economic purpose of the capital injection, and a notarised and apostilled UBO registry extract confirming direct ownership over the Korean LLC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicion of trade-based money laundering due to potential mispricing of bitumen (e.g., transaction value deviating significantly from recognised global price indices for penetration grade bitumen).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a list of comparative quotations from three independent international price reporting agencies (e.g., Platts, Argus) for the delivery month, independent third-party pre-shipment inspection certificate, standard shipping documents (Bill of Lading, Commercial Invoice, Packing List, Certificate of Origin), and the full charter party contract for the containerised movement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The Korean entity has historically minimal payroll or operational expenditure relative to the projected trade turnover, raising a managerial substance red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Demonstrate operational substance via a lease agreement for the registered office, payroll records for at least two resident employees, corporate card statements for operational expenses, and a forward-looking business plan with monthly turnover forecasts supported by purchase orders and sales contracts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital from a non-resident shareholder must be wired into a dedicated 'Capital Escrow Account' (foreign investment account) at a designated Tier-1 commercial bank. The remitting bank must include the Foreign Exchange Purpose Code 92001 (acquisition of shares of a domestic company) in the MT103. Upon receipt, the bank registers the transaction on the FEIS and issues a certificate of foreign investment, which serves as evidence for capital verification. No central bank approval is required if the transaction value is below the notification threshold; however, the notification must be submitted to the MOEF through the bank. Funds are then released into the basic operational currency account once the foreign investment report is complete and the corporate registration has been updated.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For import settlement (when the Korean LLC purchases bitumen from overseas suppliers), use SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers with Purpose Code 92011 (payment for goods) attached to the commercial invoice and Bill of Lading. To reduce counterparty risk, issue an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C at sight) through the Korean bank to the beneficiary's bank, covering the cargo value and transport charges. For discount or consignment-based transactions, utilise Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) per Incoterms. For re-export sales, the collection of export proceeds should be processed through the same FX bank with the applicable export settlement purpose code. All trade transactions must be supported by the full documentary set (invoice, packing list, transport document, insurance certificate, and customs declaration) to ensure FEIS compliance and to mitigate the risk of fines under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward contracts (USD/KRW, EUR/KRW) for trade-related receivables/payables with a maximum maturity of 12 months and underlying documentary evidence subscription
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted for non-resident counterparties or for hedging non-trade FX exposure, subject to the banks internal limits and FEIS reporting
FX swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps for multilateral treasury optimisation of the LLC's foreign currency working capital
Currency options (plain vanilla calls/puts) with a premium paid on a spot basis, used only for hedging forecasted trade flows and not for speculative positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return for the Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) filed electronically through HomeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service, Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the third month after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, by March 31 of the following year, or the next business day if the date falls on a weekend or public holiday
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Negligent-non-filing and underreporting additional taxes of 10-20% of the unpaid corporate tax depending on culpability, plus daily overdue interest of 0.022%; persistent and chronic non-compliance may trigger enforced collection and, for a dormant entity, court-ordered strike-off from the commercial register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surtax return corresponding to the national corporate income tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government of the jurisdiction in which the company is registered, using the joint national-local electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the national corporate income tax return; for a December 31 year-end, by March 31 of the following year or the next business day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local surtax late-filing and underpayment penalties plus monthly overdue interest on unpaid local tax; sustained delinquency may result in enforced seizure and cancellation of business registration under local tax collection procedures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and, when the statutory audit threshold is met, external audit report presented for approval at the members' general meeting and filed with the financial regulator
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Members' general meeting of the Yuhan Hoesa; external audit report filed with the Financial Supervisory Service through the DART electronic disclosure system; copy maintained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements and audit report must be approved within six months after fiscal year-end, i.e., by June 30 for a December 31 year-end; the auditor's report must be delivered and publicly filed within the time window prescribed by the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, generally within two weeks after delivery to the company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines and disciplinary sanctions under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; failure to prepare, retain, or approve financial statements can disqualify the audit exemption, increase tax penalties, and expose directors and officers to administrative fines; ongoing refusal may lead to court-ordered dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax declarations covering the two semi-annual taxable periods of the company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service, Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half-year period January 1 through June 30: file by July 25 of the calendar year; second half-year period July 1 through December 31: file by January 25 of the following calendar year, or the next business day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax computed at 10-20% of unpaid VAT depending on late filing, omission, or non-issuance of tax invoices, plus daily overdue interest of 0.022%; chronic unflagged operations may be administratively deregistered and the managers may be subject to criminal fines

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment ownership and membership interest movement update, applicable only if the Yuhan Hoesa has non-resident members or foreign capital in its register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy via the KOTRA foreign investment support office; capital and member changes also recorded at the competent court registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any share or membership interest transfer, capital change, foreign investment registration amendment, or change in beneficial ownership particulars; no separate mandatory calendar-year filing if no change occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines for failure to report foreign investment changes, suspension or loss of foreign-investment tax incentives, and possible correction or strike-off of inaccurate commercial register entries

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit and preservation check for the register of members, register of directors, register of charges or pledges, and minutes of members' meetings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company management with verification at each members' general meeting; registers open for inspection by members and authorized public authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Registers must be continuously updated from each corporate event and formally audited no later than the annual members' meeting, which for a December 31 year-end must occur by June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under the Korean Commercial Act for failure to maintain, preserve, or make registers available for inspection; continued non-compliance can lead to compulsory corrective court orders and, in extreme cases, judicial strike-off of the company registration

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Yuhan Hoesa must appoint a certified external auditor when total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12 billion; the Financial Services Commission may also designate a company as requiring a mandatory audit based on annual revenue, employee headcount, or public-interest transaction characteristics, in which case the same statutory audit obligations apply. The mandatory audit requirement triggers independent certified public accountant review of the complete balance sheet, income statement, statement of changes in members' equity, cash flow statement, and notes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) as the primary framework, with the Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Practices (Korean GAAP) permitted for non-listed entities that do not meet the scale requiring full K-IFRS; simplified Korean SME GAAP applies where the company qualifies for the small- and medium-sized enterprise accounting exemptions under the External Audit Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not maintain a standing public UBO registry for a private Yuhan Hoesa; however, the company must keep an accurate member register and confirm beneficial ownership at each annual members' general meeting. Any transfer of membership interests, change in ownership percentage, or variation in foreign investment particulars must be reflected in the statutory register immediately and, where foreign investment is present, reported to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through KOTRA within 30 days of the event. The company must also retain up-to-date beneficial ownership and identity documents for anti-money laundering and financial institution customer due diligence purposes for at least the statutory retention period.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 35,000 per year for a certified statutory audit and financial statement preparation, dependent on transaction volume, inventory complexity, and applicable accounting framework

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Progressive: 9% on taxable base up to KRW 200,000,000; 19% over KRW 200,000,000 to KRW 20,000,000,000; 21% over KRW 20,000,000,000 to KRW 300,000,000,000; 24% above KRW 300,000,000,000 (Corporate Income Tax Act, Article 55)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No patent box or general tax holiday for bitumen wholesale; eligible incentives include R&D tax credits under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act, job-creation tax credits, foreign-investment tax reductions under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and Free Economic Zone preferential rates for qualifying enterprises

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 2 – Corporate Tax Base and Tax Return) filed through the HomeTax electronic portal (www.hometax.go.kr) at the National Tax Service district office having jurisdiction over the head office
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; semi-annual interim tax prepayment is also required within 2 months after the first half of a fiscal year (e.g., by August 31 for calendar-year entities)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return must be filed within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (March 31 for fiscal year ending December 31); automatically extended to 5 months (May 31) for corporations subject to external audit

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – Taxpayer Identification and Corporate Profile
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity name (Yuhan Hoesa), Korean business registration number (business registration certificate), head office address, representative director, relevant fiscal year, and the local tax office assigned for filing
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare every non-resident shareholder individually, including name, country of residence, shareholding percentage, and foreign identification numbers; attach the certificate of foreign investment (foreign investment report) if an equity owner used the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; any foreign manager or beneficial owner must also be disclosed with a Tax Residency Certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 – Revenue, Cost of Sales, and Ordinary Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of total gross revenue from wholesale supply of drummed/bagged bitumen and asphalt products, cost of goods sold, selling and administrative expenses, operating income, and other non-operating income or expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Book revenue at the actual invoice price evidenced by customs declarations, Bill of Lading, and SWIFT/LC payment receipts; for all cross-border intercompany sales, state whether the price justifies an arm's-length range compared with comparable uncontrolled export prices; if the transaction is made with a related foreign entity, attach the statutory 'International Transaction Report' (Form 47) and install a cost accounting breakdown separate from any foreign logistics service fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation entries for non-deductible expenses, over-discontinued depreciation, entertainment expense additions, income exclusion/deductions, and other adjustments to convert book income into tax base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any transfer pricing adjustment demanded by the Korean tax authorities must be reflected here; when a DTA-protected offshore affiliate receives a management fee, royalty, or interest, only the actually paid amount limited to an arm's-length fee is deductible; obtain and retain a Korean transfer pricing study demonstrating the applied method and comparability adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 20 – Foreign Tax Credit (Residence Taxation) and Treaty Relief Items
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of foreign income taxes paid abroad and the credit taken, plus any foreign and domestic dividend gross-up calculations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean Yuhan Hoesa, as a resident company, may claim a direct foreign tax credit for taxes withheld on foreign-source bitumen trading proceeds; however, the entry must not include taxes withheld from non-residents. For sourced income paid to non-resident shareholders and lenders, declare the entire WHT obligation separately to prevent double counting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 27 – Withholding Tax on Non-Residents (Outbound Payments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate amount of dividends, interest, royalties, and other selves paid to non-residents from which corporate income tax is withheld, including the tax withheld and remitted to the local tax office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For every outbound remittance to a non-resident shareholder or offshore related party, list payee name, residence jurisdiction, payment amount, applicable statutory rate or treaty rate, and attach evidence of the treaty relief submission (Application for Withholding Tax Exemption or Reduction); if no withholding is performed because of a DTA exemption, the beneficial ownership and economic substance of the payee must be documented; failing to attach this evidence will trigger a 22% WHT assessment and negligence penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file by the statutory deadline triggers a non-filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax (Framework Act on National Taxes, Article 47-2); if a return is filed late but omits income, the unfaithful filing penalty is 10% of the underreported tax (Article 47-3); daily overdue interest of 0.022% per day applies to late payment; intentional false declaration can escalate to criminal fraud under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act, with fines up to three times the tax evaded and imprisonment up to 3 years (up to 5 years where the evaded amount exceeds KRW 500,000,000).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wHT_rate: 22% (20% corporate income tax + 10% local income tax surcharge on the 20% national tax, yielding 22% effective statutory rate) under Corporate Income Tax Act, Article 156
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident payee must submit a completed Application for Tax Treaty Exemption/Reduction (Withholding Tax on Non-Resident or Foreign Corporation) to the Korean withholding obligor before the payment remittance; the application must be accompanied by a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority within the relevant fiscal year, a beneficial ownership declaration stating the payee is the final owner and not a conduit, and an OECD-compliant substance questionnaire (premises, employees, and business activity); the Korean payer enters the treaty reduction in the withholding return and retains the documents. If the application is accepted after the remittance, the excess withheld tax may be reclaimed by filing a refund claim within 5 years from the statutory payment deadline.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 22% (20% national tax + 2% local surcharge); DTA rates typically reduce to 10-15%, and for IP licensing a beneficial ownership condition is mandatory. Interest: statutory 22%; treaty rates generally range from 10% to 15%, with OECD-compliant preferential interest article for financial institutions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 5,000,000,000 in a fiscal year; Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue is at least KRW 1,000,000,000,000; Country-by-Country Report is triggered at the same consolidated revenue threshold (KRW 1 trillion) when group revenue exceeds KRW 1,000,000,000,000
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea applies the OECD substance-over-form doctrine and the abuse-of-rights principle in taxation; a Yuhan Hoesa with no real office, no employees, no inventory risk, and no decision-making power in the bitumen wholesale trade will be treated as a transparent shell and its transactions will be disregarded or recharacterized. Beneficial ownership is required to access DTA benefits, and the Korean CFC rules under Article 17 of the International Tax Adjustment Act attribute undistributed offshore income to the Korean entity if the economic substance is merely a paper intermediary.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion via Fraudulent Transfer Pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling containerized bitumen to a related Hong Kong or Singapore shell entity at a 30-40% discount to the prevailing market price while recording an equally inflated service fee to the same offshore party, thereby shifting the Korean Yuhan Hoesa's taxable profit out of Korea and creating false customs and inventory documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment under the International Tax Adjustment Act (ITAA) Article 5 to the arm's-length price; an adjustment penalty of 10% of the unreported taxable income under ITAA Article 13; criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act (PTOA) Article 3, imposing a fine of up to three times the evaded tax and imprisonment of up to 3 years; if the evaded tax amount exceeds KRW 500,000,000, imprisonment increases up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The tax authority may invoke secondary tax liability under Articles 38-40 of the Framework Act on National Taxes to pierce the corporate veil and seize a director's personal bank deposits, vehicles, and residential property; the responsible director who signed the false invoices is personally subject to criminal penalty with imprisonment of up to 5 years and a permanent blacklisting on the Korean tax offender public registry, leading to immigration travel bans and disqualification as a director for 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Willful Failure to Withhold Non-Resident Tax on Dividends and Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring and remitting a KRW 1,000,000,000 dividend to the non-resident parent and a KRW 500,000,000 royalty to a related Jersey/Germany entity without any withholding, and omitting these payments from the withholding tax return despite the absence of an approved treaty exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Income Tax Act Article 156 obligates the Korean payer to withhold; in default, the tax is collected directly from the payer, plus a penalty of 10% of the non-collected amount under Article 47-3, plus 0.022% daily late-payment interest; additionally, under Article 29 of the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act, the representative can be fined up to KRW 100,000,000 or imprisoned for up to 2 years for failing to perform withholding duties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors serving as statutory withholding agents are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid WHT and penalties; if the company is insolvent, the National Tax Service can seize a director's personal property through secondary liability proceedings; criminal conviction leads to personal criminal record, a travel ban, and forfeiture of profits placed in personal accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse and Lack of Economic Substance to Claim DTA Benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Korean Yuhan Hoesa as a pure letterbox entity: no employees, no independent software or physical storage of bitumen, no negotiation authority, and using the Korean entity solely to claim the Korea-Hong Kong DTA on outbound royalties paid to an offshore intellectual-property holding company, with all purchase and sale decisions actually made in a foreign jurisdiction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief under the beneficial ownership principle (ITAA Article 11) and the OECD BEPS Action 6 minimum standard; the company is reassessed at the statutory 22% withholding tax, plus a 30% negligence penalty for unjustified understatement; if the Korean entity is held to be a sham, the tax authority can invalidate its tax refunds; the Korean Anti-Money Laundering Act (Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Information) may also apply for conducting foreign transactions through a shell without a real beneficial owner registry
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are civilly liable for the additional WHT and penalties, and a court may pierce the corporate veil based on fraud (Criminal Act Article 347); if the director used the shell company to launder bitumen sales proceeds, the director faces up to 10 years imprisonment, an asset forfeiture order, and an immediate no-exit immigration order; repeated violations trigger director disqualification under the Commercial Act Article 398 and revocation of the corporate business license.
